correctness.rationale: The proof gives explicit comparable-map zigzags in both branches. A singleton occupied target level contracts the image. Without singleton levels, the two points of each source level must map to two distinct points of one target level, and source-level order forces these target levels to be strictly increasing. Thus excess source height forces the first branch; deficit source height leaves an unused target level whose point contracts the image inclusion. The exhaustive checker confirms the dichotomy and a single mapping-space component in six representative unequal-height cases.

value.rationale: The result separates finite-space homotopy from classical homotopy after taking order complexes. It gives an exact structural obstruction in the actual finite mapping space, showing that unequal-dimensional minimal sphere models have only the constant homotopy class of direct maps and extending the mechanism to arbitrary noncontractible weak-order targets of different height. This is a natural boundary for finite models of maps rather than a routine count or parameter substitution.
